section_summary: This section moves from 1941 assessments of Japanese and Japanese-American newspapers—including censorship of the Japan News Week and the political alignment of the Japan Times and Advertiser—to wartime correspondence about press consolidation, historical newspaper issues, and overseas Japanese news services. Most of the section consists of November 1943 Dōmei Agency bulletins circulated in Turkey, combining exaggerated Japanese victory claims with reports promoting the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, collaborationist governments, Indian independence, and Japanese administration in occupied territories. The bulletins also document Japanese propaganda concerning the Greater East Asia Conference, fighting around Bougainville and New Guinea, and political developments across East and Southeast Asia.

subfiles.title: Review of Japanese and Japanese-American press coverage
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese press arguments on China, Australia, Japanese-American relations, and the American national emergency, followed by an assessment of Japanese-American publications.
subfiles.summary: Press review: claims Japan would permit Western enterprise in China, Australia favored cooperation, and a U.S.-Japan accord could end the China conflict; Japanese American coverage of Roosevelt's emergency declaration; the Review is overtly pro-American, while the Japanese American appeals to older immigrants through pan-Asian and Buddhist themes.

subfiles.title: Telegram 1446 concerning censorship of the Japan News Week
subfiles.about: Reports official threats against editor Ward H. Wills after an editorial criticized Hitler and suggested that Nazi Germany might be defeated.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 1446: censors passed foreign dispatches on the Japan News Week editorial, then banned the issue; officials told Wills it attacked Japan's fundamental policy and criticism could mean suppression or prison, and he said he'd stop publishing rather than turn it into a propaganda sheet.

subfiles.title: Memorandum and Millard letter excerpt on the Japan Times and Advertiser
subfiles.about: Assesses Thomas Millard’s claim that Matsuoka-aligned interests purchased the Japan Advertiser to influence Japanese foreign policy.
subfiles.summary: The memo finds the claim plausible given Toshi Go's ties to Matsuoka and the South Manchuria Railway; Millard's excerpt says the Times and Advertiser promoted Matsuoka, a U.S. visit, cooperation on China and compromise with Chiang, and that the military controls Tokyo's government.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference for Kaigai Dōbō
subfiles.about: Points to a translated copy of the first issue of Kaigai Dōbō, published by the Overseas Japanese Central Society.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to an October 11, 1941 Justice letter with a translation of Kaigai Dobo's first issue (July 15, 1941); see the Overseas Japanese Central Society file.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference for Japanese seven-point program
subfiles.about: Cross-references instructions for commenting on a truculent seven-point Japanese program published in the Japan Times and Advertiser.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram 4716 (November 5, 1941) on a Japanese seven-point list of demands, suggesting stressing to the Foreign Office the press's uncompromising tone.

subfiles.title: Amalgamation of the Tokyo Nichi Nichi and Osaka Mainichi
subfiles.from: James W. Gantenbein, U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Reports that two major Japanese newspapers merged as the Mainichi Shimbun, probably because of paper shortages.
subfiles.summary: A report says the Tokyo Nichi Nichi and Osaka Mainichi began appearing as the Mainichi Shimbun January 1, 1943; the embassy thinks paper shortages caused it and names Saburo Suzuki as the Buenos Aires representative of both.

subfiles.title: Lillian J. Mitchell’s letter sending 1920 Japan Advertiser issues
subfiles.about: Offers several 1920 newspaper issues whose editorial discussion of land ownership in Japan might interest the President.
subfiles.summary: Lillian Mitchell mails old 1920 newspapers, especially an editorial on land in Japan, and offers Roosevelt encouragement in a time of trial.

subfiles.title: Analysis of October 1920 Japan Advertiser issues
subfiles.about: Reviews the editorials and translated articles in the newspaper issues supplied by Lillian J. Mitchell.
subfiles.summary: Analysis of October 1920 Japan Advertiser issues: a Tokyo Nichinichi editorial urges moderation on American land and immigration laws, plus the Hunchun Incident, criticism of incursions into China and a missionary's account of harsh treatment of Koreans; historically significant for 1920's relatively critical press.

subfiles.title: Reply to Lillian J. Mitchell
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Mitchell’s letter and the October 1920 Japan Advertiser issues she supplied.
subfiles.summary: State tells Mitchell her letter to the President and the newspapers were referred to it; Salisbury thanks her for her helpful spirit.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese foreign-language newspapers in occupied territories
subfiles.about: Relays a German press report on Japanese agencies’ extensive foreign-language newspaper operations in occupied Asia.
subfiles.summary: Telegram lists Domei, Asahi and Mainichi papers in Singapore, Malaya, Java, the Philippines, Celebes and Hainan, notes Manila, Java, Celebes and Shonan Shimbun as important, evening foreign-language papers reuse morning Japanese editions, and English papers are seen as temporary.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Dōmei News Bulletins from Turkey
subfiles.about: Advises that Washington already receives equivalent Dōmei material through federal broadcast-monitoring reports.
subfiles.summary: Kohler says Japanese Affairs checked whether Berry's Domei bulletins were unique; the FCC's Broadcast Intelligence Service already issues daily reports on the same material for Washington agencies.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese Dōmei News Bulletins in Turkey
subfiles.from: Burton Y. Berry, American Consul General, Istanbul
subfiles.about: Forwards privately obtained November issues of the Japanese Dōmei news bulletin and asks whether the Department already receives the information elsewhere.
subfiles.summary: Berry sends November's daily Japanese Domei bulletins from Turkey, covering more than military communiques, hopes the private source continues, and asks guidance if State already gets equivalent reporting.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin, Ankara, November 4—French edition
subfiles.about: Reports Fascist organization in Japan, Free India diplomacy, military claims in Burma, fundraising in Malaya, physical education in Indochina, and Japanese–Thai cooperation.
subfiles.summary: Domei bulletin, Ankara, November 4 (French): Italian Fascists in Kobe reorganize under Gennaro Liguori, Free India thanks Mitsuru Toyama and Chu Minyi, a claimed victory near Myitkyina, Overseas Chinese funding aircraft in Johor Bahru, and Indochina physical education.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 4—English edition
subfiles.about: Combines diplomatic, military, ideological, and economic reports from China, Burma, the South Pacific, and Celebes.
subfiles.summary: Domei bulletin, Ankara, November 4 (English): Masayuki Tani arrives in Shanghai, claims on Tankakok and Pomele, a Shanghai editorial presenting the Sino-Japanese alliance as the road to independence, and a Makassar item praising Japanese progress in Manado and Minahasa.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin on the Greater East Asia Conference
subfiles.about: Describes the Greater East Asia Conference in Tokyo and reproduces the central themes of speeches by Tōjō and Wang Jingwei.
subfiles.summary: Bulletin on the Greater East Asia Conference: seating, delegates and ceremony; Tojo denounces Anglo-American colonialism and presents Japan as architect of a new East Asian order; Wang Jingwei praises Japan, invokes Sun Yat-sen and urges sovereignty, culture, harmony and mutual economic aid.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 5—South Pacific military commentary
subfiles.about: Presents Japanese claims about ground and naval operations in the Solomon Islands and argues that Allied supply lines made their South Pacific campaign untenable.
subfiles.summary: A field report claims that a Japanese reconnaissance party repelled a larger force near Choiseul without casualties. Two commentaries describe Finschhafen, Bougainville, Rabaul, and Buin as scenes of disastrous Allied attacks. The analysis emphasizes allegedly overstretched American supply lines and asserts continuing Japanese command of the sea.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 8, with erratum
subfiles.about: Claims sweeping Japanese naval victories, announces the proposed transfer of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to Free India, and reports political activity across East and Southeast Asia.
subfiles.summary: Domei, Ankara, November 8: inflated Allied ship and aircraft losses at Bougainville and Rabaul, Tojo's promise to give the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to Bose's government, Lin Posheng in Tokyo, Padang Indian mobilization, Emilio Abello's support; erratum "battle cruiser" to "heavy cruiser."

subfiles.title: Detached Dōmei bulletin leaf on Ichang and Haiphong
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese counterattacks near Ichang and an American air raid on Haiphong.
subfiles.summary: Detached Domei leaf: Japanese units repelled two attacks near Lungchuanpao and recovered arms, and six American P-40s strafed Haiphong's outskirts without Japanese losses.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin on the Battle of Bougainville
subfiles.about: Publishes an Imperial General Headquarters communiqué claiming major naval and air victories around Bougainville.
subfiles.summary: Communique on the Battle of Bougainville, October 31-November 3: claimed cruisers and destroyers sunk or damaged between Mono and Bougainville, fighting at Torokina, and 200 aircraft destroyed at Rabaul and 39 at Buka.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin, Ankara, November 8—French edition
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese air operations, Indian nationalist activity, an Italian Fascist office in Tokyo, and preparations for a Greater East Asia press conference.
subfiles.summary: Domei, Ankara, November 8 (French): claimed attacks at Nadzab, Finschhafen, Munda, Biloa, Vella Lavella and Torokina; Saigon Indians' support for Free India; Omero Principini's new office for Italian Fascist interests; southern journalists passing Shonan for Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 8—English edition
subfiles.about: Covers Shanghai finance, Manchukuo diplomacy, Japanese air claims in New Guinea, and the training of Malay auxiliaries in Shōnan.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin reports the reopening of Shanghai’s clearing house and Zhang Jinghui’s return to Hsinking. It gives detailed but propagandistic figures for Japanese raids on Nadzab and fighting near Finschhafen. A long feature portrays Malay heiho auxiliaries as enthusiastic, disciplined, physically fit, and well cared for by Japanese commanders.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 9
subfiles.about: Reports Philippine economic rhetoric, Japanese claims of American naval defeat, and the creation of provincial councils under occupation in Sumatra.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 9: Benigno Aquino urges Filipinos to pair independence with economic stability; Tokyo commentary treats American silence as proof of Solomons losses with enormous claimed totals; Sumatra provincial councils and welfare bureaus advertise self-government under military control.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin, Ankara, November 10—Bougainville supplement
subfiles.about: Adds further Japanese victory claims for Bougainville and records congratulatory and propaganda reactions in Japan, Chungking, and Burma.
subfiles.summary: Bougainville supplement, November 10: headquarters claims another battleship sunk and more cruisers damaged; Okada congratulates Admiral Koga; Reuters' relay of the claims is read as Chungking's reluctant recognition; an Indian National Army officer welcomes the Andaman and Nicobar transfer.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin on Free India recognition and regional news
subfiles.about: Reports Italian Fascist recognition of Free India, revised Japanese air claims, and a planned medical conference in Manila.
subfiles.summary: Domei: Principini completes Italian Fascist recognition of Free India's Provisional Government, claimed Allied aircraft losses at Rabaul rise, an Ambon interception, and Laurel accepts the presidency of a Manila medical-scientific conference.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 10
subfiles.about: Reports official congratulations and presents Wang Jingwei’s and Zhang Jinghui’s ideological defenses of the Greater East Asia Conference.
subfiles.summary: Domei, Ankara, November 10: Zhang Jinghui, Okada and Tojo celebrate the conference declaration and naval claims; Wang Jingwei contrasts its principles with Vienna and Versailles and urges Chongqing to abandon the Anglo-Americans; Zhang calls it a sincere anti-imperialist alliance.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 11
subfiles.about: Describes public celebration of Japanese victory claims, diplomatic congratulations, Bose’s anti-British speech, Macao currency controls, and estimates of Allied casualties.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 11: jubilant Filipinos, Zhang Jinghui's congratulations, Bose rejecting compromise with Britain at a Tokyo gathering, Macao banning Chinese twenty-cent coins, and a calculation of over 10,000 Allied personnel lost from speculative crew figures.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin, Ankara, November 11
subfiles.about: Reports fighting near Bougainville and in Hunan, Bose’s visits to Japanese admirals, Manchukuo congratulations, and Philippine constitutional festivities.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 11: another fleet action off Bougainville, a Japanese advance in the Dongting Lake region, Bose congratulating Admirals Nagano and Shimada, Zhang Jinghui's message to Tojo, and plans for a three-day Philippine constitution celebration.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 12
subfiles.about: Covers a Greater East Asian youth conference and ceremonies commemorating Sun Yat-sen in occupied China and Shōnan.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 12: youth from Japan, Manchukuo, China, Burma and Hitler Youth meet in Tokyo; Wang Jingwei uses Sun Yat-sen's birthday to praise war on Britain and the U.S. and the Sino-Japanese alliance; parallel ceremonies in Shanghai, Peking and Shonan.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin, Ankara, November 12—French edition
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese action in Central China and collaborationist commemorations of Sun Yat-sen in Nanking and Canton.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 12 (French): claimed annihilation of about 500 Chinese troops, and Nanking and Canton ceremonies with Wang Jingwei presenting the Japan alliance and Greater East Asia declaration as fulfilling Sun Yat-sen's ideals.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 13
subfiles.about: Reports Indian military trainees, Philippine family statistics, and allegations of hostility between American and Chungking air officers.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 13: Bose picks six Penang youths for training in Japan, Manila household statistics, and testimony of a captured Chinese lieutenant alleging American arrogance and quarrels with Chinese air officers at Yunnanyi, evidently meant to undermine Sino-American cooperation.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 15
subfiles.about: Combines reports of Japanese operations in Hebei and the Solomons with Mamoru Shigemitsu’s ideological address on Asian independence.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 15: claimed capture of Wang Lienfang in a raid on an Eighth Route Army headquarters, air attacks on Mono and Torokina, and Shigemitsu in Osaka calling the Greater East Asia declaration a charter for a new world and the war Asia's struggle against colonialism.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin, Ankara, November 16—condolences and military reports
subfiles.about: Reports imperial condolences for the French ambassador and Japanese military claims from Hunan, Ichang, and Haiphong.
subfiles.summary: The emperor and empress send representatives or messages to the French Embassy after Ambassador Charles Arsène-Henry’s death. Military reports claim Japanese successes along the Canton–Hankou railway and near Yueyang, Taolin, Ichang, and Lungchuanpao. A final item says American P-40 aircraft strafed Haiphong without inflicting Japanese damage.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin, Ankara, November 16—evening reports
subfiles.about: Reports South Pacific air operations, an action against Communist troops in Hebei, honors for Javanese leaders, telegraph expansion, and Japanese naval appointments.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 16 evening: claimed attacks around the Gilbert, Bougainville, Mono and Ellice islands, Wang Lienfang's capture in Hebei, decorations and an imperial audience for Sukarno, Bohol and Tarlac telegraph service, and Sasebo and naval aviation appointments.

subfiles.title: Dōmei Information Bulletin, Ankara, November 17
subfiles.about: Announces another purported Japanese air victory off Bougainville and reports interceptions near Madang, Nauru, Hanoi, and Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 17: headquarters claims naval aircraft sank three carriers and other warships south of Bougainville in a Fifth Air Battle, plus bombers shot down near Madang and Nauru; Hanoi and Hong Kong report American aircraft driven off.

subfiles.title: Dōmei News Bulletin, Ankara, November 17—English edition
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese cabinet appointments, expands victory claims from Bougainville, and announces a new Thai military attaché in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 17 (English): Teiichi Suzuki, Yoshisuke Aikawa and Keita Goto named cabinet advisers after Fujiwara resigned; claimed decisive attack on an Allied carrier force and enormous 20-day loss totals; Nomsak Pholarak replaces Solakit Phisien as Thai attache in Tokyo.
